author: EmuCore - Hub
title: DuckStation's MMPXEnhanced rewrite targets bubble-free pixel-art scaling
summary: Approximate color matching and expanded shape rules replace much of the earlier scaler, adding transition detail while attacking the rounded bubbles created around four-pixel intersections.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from DuckStation pull request #3717: MMPXEnhanced v3.0

blocks.text: Exact color equality misses structure in textured pixel art

Pixel-art scalers often infer edges by comparing neighboring colors. Strict equality works on flat sprites but loses detail when shading, compression, or deliberate dithering produces close rather than identical values. MMPXEnhanced 3.0 introduces approximate-pixel comparisons so its shape rules can recognize related regions without treating every small color difference as a boundary that must remain blocky.
Mixed pixels create transitions the source pattern implies

The rewrite can generate intermediate colors where neighboring regions indicate a transition. Expanded morphological functions then decide how those samples form corners, diagonals, and outlines. The author reports that most of the core algorithm was rewritten, with particular attention to the bubble artifacts created where four source pixels intersect. The goal is controlled shape reconstruction, not arbitrary blur over the entire frame.
Shared ports provide evidence, but DuckStation's shader path still matters

Versions of the algorithm were already available for libretro and PPSSPP, giving the rules exposure on other shader systems before this integration. DuckStation places the work in its hardware shader generator, so compilation, precision, and sampling behavior still require local validation. Similar output on another emulator is useful reference material, but it does not prove identical coordinates or performance in DuckStation.
Quality and cost should be measured at 2x before scaling higher

The source recommends 2x for 2D games and warns that the additional conditionals make 4x or 3D use heavy without a fast GPU. Tests should include thin diagonals, checkerboards, four-color intersections, text, transparency, and animated scrolling. Compare the older MMPX result, version 3.0, and nearest-neighbor output, then record GPU time at 2x and 4x. Fewer bubbles should not come at the cost of unstable edges or missed details.
MMPXEnhanced 3.0 trades shader simplicity for richer shape judgment; its natural target is 2x pixel-art scaling, not every 3D scene at maximum resolution.
